questions.question: The price of a television set and a washing machine are in the ratio of 8 : 7. If the cost of the television set is ₹4,800 more than the cost of the washing machine, then find the price of the washing machine.
questions.questionHtml: The price of a television set and a washing machine are in the ratio of 8 : 7. If the cost of the television set is ₹4,800 more than the cost of the washing machine, then find the price of the washing machine.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of price of Television (TV) to Washing Machine (WM) = 8 : 7.

Difference in ratio parts = 8 − 7 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = ₹4,800.

Price of Washing Machine = 7 units = 7 × ₹4,800.

Price of Washing Machine = ₹33,600.

∴ The correct answer is ₹33,600.

Alternate Method

Given → Price Ratio = 8 : 7 | Difference = ₹4,800. Formulas: Price = Ratio Part × Constant Value (x).
⇒ Let the price of Television be 8x and Washing Machine be 7x. ⇒ According to the question: 8x − 7x = 4,800. ⇒ x = 4,800. ⇒ Price of Washing Machine = 7x = 7 × 4,800. ⇒ Price = ₹33,600.

∴ The correct answer is ₹33,600.

Additional Information

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities by division. If a : b is the ratio, the actual values can be represented as ax and bx where x is a common multiplier.

Unitary Method

This method involves finding the value of a single unit and then multiplying it by the required number of units to find the total value.

questions.question: A shopkeepers made a profit of 16% on his goods. If the price at which he buys decreases by 20% while he reduces his selling price by 23%, what is now his percentage of profit? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeepers made a profit of 16% on his goods. If the price at which he buys decreases by 20% while he reduces his selling price by 23%, what is now his percentage of profit? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Given:

A shopkeepers made a profit of 16% on his goods.

Formula Used:

profit = selling price - cost price 

Calculation:

Let his cost price = Rs. 100x

⇒ Selling price to get 16% profit = \(\frac{116}{100}\) × 100x = Rs. 116x

⇒ Now, new cost price = \(\frac{80}{100} × 100x = Rs. 80x\)

⇒ New selling price = \(\frac{77}{100} × 116x = Rs. 89.32x \)

∴ New Profit % = \(\frac{89.32x - 80x}{80x}\) × 100

⇒ \(\frac{9.32}{4} \times 5 = 11.6%\)

∴ required profit = 11.6 %

questions.question: Dinesh purchases 12 dozens of apples at the rate of Rs. 300 per dozen. He sells each apple at the rate of Rs. 30. What is the profit of Dinesh?
questions.questionHtml: Dinesh purchases 12 dozens of apples at the rate of Rs. 300 per dozen. He sells each apple at the rate of Rs. 30. What is the profit of Dinesh?
questions.solution:
Given:

Dinesh purchases 12 dozens of apples at ₹300 per dozen.

He sells each apple at ₹30.

Solution:

Step 1: Calculate the total cost price:

Cost Price = 12 × 300 = ₹3600

Step 2: Calculate the total selling price:

Total apples = 12 × 12 = 144 apples

Selling Price = 144 × 30 = ₹4320

Step 3: Calculate the profit:

Profit = ₹4320 - ₹3600 = ₹720

Profit % = (720 × 100)/3600 = 20%

∴ Dinesh's profit is 20%.

Increase of cost through two middlemen each gaining 25%

⇒ X × (125/100) × (125/100) = Rs 625000 ⇒ X = (625000 × 16) /25 = Rs 400000

questions.question: A man bought apples at the rate of 8 apples for Rs. 34 and sold them at the rate of 12 apples for Rs.57. How many apples should be sold to earn a net profit of Rs.45?
questions.questionHtml: A man bought apples at the rate of 8 apples for Rs. 34 and sold them at the rate of 12 apples for Rs.57. How many apples should be sold to earn a net profit of Rs.45?
questions.solution: CP of 24 apples = 34 × 3 = Rs. 102 SP of 24 apples = 57 × 2 = Rs. 114 Profit on 24 apples = 114 - 102 = Rs. 12 Number of apples for Rs. 45 profit = (24 / 12) × 45 = 90 apples

questions.question: A real estate agent sells a site to Amit for Rs 1,80,000 at a profit of 25% and Amit sells it to Sukhi at a profit of 10%. What is the cost price of Sukhi?
questions.questionHtml: A real estate agent sells a site to Amit for Rs 1,80,000 at a profit of 25% and Amit sells it to Sukhi at a profit of 10%. What is the cost price of Sukhi?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Agent sold to Amit (SP) = 180000

Real estate sells to Amit at Profit% = 25%

Amit sells to Sukhi at Profit% = 10%

Calculation:

Here, SP for Amit = CP of Sukhi = 1,80,000

⇒ CP for Sukhi = 1,80,000 × (110/100)

⇒ CP for Sukhi = 1,98,000

The correct answer is 1,98,000.

questions.question: A wholesaler sells a tin of oil at Rs. 540 and bears a loss of 10%. Now, if he decides to sell another tin of oil with same cost at Rs. 696, his profit percentage in the sale of second tin will be equal to:
questions.questionHtml: A wholesaler sells a tin of oil at Rs. 540 and bears a loss of 10%. Now, if he decides to sell another tin of oil with same cost at Rs. 696, his profit percentage in the sale of second tin will be equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Loss of 10% means 90% of Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 540.

Ratio of Selling Prices to percentages: 540 ⇒ 90%.

Unitary method: 1 ⇒ 90 ÷ 540 = 1/6%.

For New Selling Price Rs. 696: 696 ⇒ 696 × (1/6)% = 116%.

Profit percentage = 116% − 100% = 16%.

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Alternate Method

Given: First SP = Rs. 540, Loss = 10%, Second SP = Rs. 696.

Formulas: CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%], Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = (540 × 100) ÷ (100 − 10) = (540 × 100) ÷ 90 = 6 × 100 = Rs. 600.

⇒ New Profit = New SP − CP = 696 − 600 = Rs. 96.

⇒ Profit Percentage = (96 ÷ 600) × 100 = 16%.

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Additional Information

Relationship between SP, CP, and Profit/Loss

Profit occurs when Selling Price is greater than Cost Price. Loss occurs when Cost Price is greater than Selling Price.

Base for Percentage Calculation

Both Profit% and Loss% are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise in the problem.

questions.question: Zeal sells a dress to Sonia at 20% profit and Sonia sells it to rim by making 50% profit. Rim pays Rs. 6444 for the dress, what would be the cost price for zeal?
questions.questionHtml: Zeal sells a dress to Sonia at 20% profit and Sonia sells it to rim by making 50% profit. Rim pays Rs. 6444 for the dress, what would be the cost price for zeal?
questions.solution:
Cost price for Rim is the selling price for Sonia

⇒ S.P = C.P + profit

⇒ 6444 = C.P (for Sonia) + 50% of C.P

⇒ 6444 = 150 × C.P/100

⇒ C.P = 4296

C.P for Sonia is the selling price for zeal.

⇒ S.P = C.P (for zeal) + profit

⇒ 4296 = C.P + 20% profit

⇒ 4296 = 120 × C.P/100

∴ C.P = 3580

questions.question: A bought an article for Rs. 6200 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With this amount another article is bought and sold it at a gain of 30%. What was his overall gain or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A bought an article for Rs. 6200 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With this amount another article is bought and sold it at a gain of 30%. What was his overall gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

A bought an article for Rs.6200 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With this amount another article is bought and sold it at a gain of 30%

Formula used:

Profit = (SP - CP)

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100

Loss = (CP - SP)

Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100

Calculation:

CP of the article = Rs.6200

Loss = 20%

SP of the article = 80 × 6200/100

⇒ Rs. 4960

CP of second article = Rs. 4960

Gain % = 30%

SP of second article = Rs. 130 × 4960/100

⇒ 6448

Gain % = (6448 - 6200) × 100/6200

⇒ 4

∴ the correct answer is 4%
